people.paul.role: Writer who left Timothy at Ephesus to correct teachers
people.paul.relations: He calls Timothy his true child in faith. He names Hymenaeus and Alexander as men he handed over.
people.paul.meaning: Paul says he urged Timothy to stay at Ephesus. He calls himself a past blasphemer and persecutor who received mercy. He gives rules for prayer, overseers, widows, and the rich. He hopes to come to Timothy soon.
people.timothy.role: Paul’s true child, told to stay at Ephesus
people.timothy.relations: Paul calls him his true child in faith and his child Timothy.
people.timothy.meaning: Paul tells Timothy to stay at Ephesus. He is to stop certain men from teaching a different doctrine. Paul tells him not to let anyone despise his youth. He is to read, exhort, and teach. He is to guard what was entrusted to him.
people.jesus.role: Lord and one mediator between God and men
people.jesus.relations: Paul calls him our hope and the man Christ Jesus. He says Jesus testified before Pontius Pilate.
people.jesus.meaning: Paul says Christ Jesus came to save sinners, and Paul is chief of them. Paul says Jesus gave himself as a ransom for all. Paul charges Timothy to keep the commandment until Jesus appears.
people.adam.role: First man formed, named in a reason for teaching rules
people.adam.relations: Paul names him just before Eve. He says Adam was formed first.
people.adam.meaning: In chapter 2 Paul says he does not permit a woman to teach. He adds that she may not have authority over a man. As his reason, Paul says Adam was formed first. Paul also says Adam was not deceived. Paul does not name a local dispute.
people.eve.role: First woman, named in a reason for teaching rules
people.eve.relations: Paul names her just after Adam. He says she was formed after him and was deceived.
people.eve.meaning: In chapter 2 Paul gives a reason for his rule about women teaching. He says Adam was formed first, then Eve. He says the woman was deceived and fell into disobedience. Paul does not name a local incident.
places.ephesus.summary: Paul urges Timothy to stay at Ephesus in chapter 1. Timothy is to stop certain men from teaching a different doctrine.
places.ephesus.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
sources.web.summary: The full Scripture text is the main text for original close readings.
sources.web.limits: Paul is the named writer. The guide did not check authorship, dates, Greek forms, or manuscripts. It did not check the local causes of the rules for women. It did not check the childbirth phrase. It names no local incident behind those rules.
sources.eberhart-timothy.summary: Eberhart separates love of money from owning things. He stresses generous use.
sources.eberhart-timothy.limits: This is Eberhart’s own reading. The guide did not check his Greek analysis or his Roman economic claims. It did not check his proposed payment of Tertius. It did not check the books he cites.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-44.summary: The lesson links sound teaching with a faithful personal example.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-44.limits: First Timothy coverage follows what the lesson discusses in chapters one, four, and six. The guide did not check the linked talks or Restoration passages.
sources.net-acts-map.summary: Opening descriptions and coordinates mark the cities named in Acts.
sources.net-acts-map.limits: These broad points do not confirm ancient events, travel paths, buildings, or coastlines. The guide did not adopt older encyclopedia claims about authorship, law, population, or exact dates.
